text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Chain of blunders in building and approval of collapsed bridge.
- Senior Palestinian officer activated "police cell" arrested two days ago on way to attack.
- Stoppages expected today at Ben Gurion airport.
- Cabinet to decide today whether to approve chemical weapons treaty.
JERUSALEM POST
- Bridge engineer: I aproved 100 person limit; Australian delegation decides to stay.
- Katyusha falls in Western Galilee.
- Six hundred million shekel budget cut to come before cabinet.
- Communications Minister Limor LIvnat: Bezeq must give refund.
MAARIV
- Bridge built without approval against the law.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met with Indyk to discuss chances of renewal of talks with Syria.
- Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa: "Netanyahu can't be believed."
HAARETZ
- Accusations traded between those responsible for collpased bridge.
- Wide majority for U.N. proposal against settlements.
- Katyusha falls in Israeli territory, Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai orders to respond with restraint.
- Netanyahu doesn't rule out possibility of tax hike.
- Jerusalem Mayor Ehud Olmert: destruction of houses will resume in October with help of special police force.
- Infrastructure Ministry chief resigns over Minister Ariel Sharon's management style.
- Health workers intend to strike all hospitals Sunday.
